blocks.text: Derive both complete paths from the supplied state

The array is already sorted, so one run scan visits every one of the n values once: run time is O(n). It retains only the current key and count, so run auxiliary space is O(1), excluding emitted output.

Rebuilding a frequency table also processes n values with one expected O(1) update each, so expected hash time is O(n). It retains one entry per distinct key, giving O(k) auxiliary space. Thus hashing is not asymptotically faster here and uses more working state, while the scan emits ordered groups directly. Reusable rule: equal time bounds do not imply equal space or equal usefulness of the produced structure.

feedback.reason: Both paths are linear in time under the stated model, so the hash path is not asymptotically faster.
